chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That two men disputed before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding a beast of burden that was in their possession, and each of them presented evidence that it had given birth at his place. He swore them both; one swore and the other refused to swear, so he ruled in favor of the one who swore. It was said to him, 'What if neither had it in his possession and both presented evidence?' He said, 'I would swear them both; whichever one swore and the other refused, I would give it to the one who swore. If both swore, I would divide it between them into two halves.' It was said, 'What if it was in the possession of one of them and both presented evidence?' He said, 'I would rule in favor of the one who swore and was in possession of it.'

key_terms.أَحْلَفَهُمَا: He made them both swear oaths

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali rule on property disputes when both parties claim ownership and one refuses to take an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the jurisprudential rules for resolving conflicting claims over a beast, emphasizing the principle of 'al-yamin' (oath) as the decisive factor when evidence is equal. It highlights the practical application of judicial discretion, where possession combined with an oath secures the ruling, reflecting the Shia emphasis on procedural justice and the weight of sworn testimony in civil disputes. The narration underscores the Imam's role in clarifying legal nuances that prevent arbitrary judgments in property conflicts.
